column3: NASB follows the critical text (“brethren”); it renders the oath particle as “I protest … by” and moves “I die daily” to the end.
NASB renders “according to man” as “from human motives”; the quotation is in capitals.
NASB renders “companionships” as “company” and puts the proverb in quotation marks. A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB renders “righteously” as “as you ought,” “do not sin” as “stop sinning,” and “ignorance of God” as “no knowledge of God.”
NASB renders “if it may be” as “perhaps.”
NASB renders “in decay … in immortality” as “a perishable body … an imperishable body.”
The quotation is in capitals except “The first” and “Adam,” which are Paul's additions.
NASB follows the critical text without “the Lord”; “made of dust” is rendered “earthy.”
NASB follows the critical text; “decay” is rendered “the perishable.”
NASB follows the critical text with both clauses; the quotation is in capitals except “in victory,” and “word” is rendered “saying.”
NASB follows the critical text (“victory … sting”); the quotation is in capitals.
